summary: Emergency throttle + unwind assistance: tenant Medibrix seeing 95p latency spikes after mixed quant + prefetch profile
description: Issue summary: After applying a mixed-quant + aggressive KV-prefetch profile for Medibrix's Dedicated cluster, they observed large 95th/99th percentile tail latency spikes and intermittent stream disconnects for long-context chat sessions. Impact: High-production customer reporting degraded user experience on their triage/chat product; ~12% of requests hitting 95p > 1.5s above baseline and occasional 5xx streaming terminations. Environment: Dedicated (reserved) cluster for Medibrix in us-east-1, pinned model redwood/gpt-open-rt-13b-quant, optimizer profile: mixed-quant-high-prefetch-v2. Key ask: Provide step-by-step safe throttle/unwind guidance that preserves throughput while minimizing customer-visible errors and rollback risk.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send chat requests with average input length ~1,200 tokens and temperature 0.2 to the tenant's pinned route.
2) Observe streaming responses for multi-turn sessions (10+ turns) where KV cache prefetch is active and batch sizes reach 8-12.
3) Note increased latency on tails (95p/99p) and occasional stream disconnects with HTTP 502/504 during long responses.
4) Revert to previous optimizer snapshot (if available) in a staging test to validate latency improvement before production change.
observed_logs: 2026-03-12T15:12:03Z tenant=medibrix route=chat-annotate model=gpt-open-rt-13b-quant latency_p95=1724ms p99=3120ms errors=2/120
k8s: pod/serve-rt-13b-quant-7c9fc logs show repeated mutex contention in kv-prefetch worker at 15:10:58Z
nginx: upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.2.4.11, server: route-chat
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: Mixed quant path increases compute variance + aggressive KV prefetch increases memory pressure leading to GC/eviction churn on the serving node.
Observed correlation between batch size peaks (>=8) and latency spikes; lower-batch requests did not show same severity.
No network-level anomalies detected between gateway and serving nodes; errors coincide with model runtime logs referencing kernel fallbacks.
Heap metrics on pod show transient OOM-kernel triggers followed by container restart in one node (restart count +1), suggests memory-exhaustion under prefetch load.
Related runbook: see Confluence page 'Optimizer Profile Rollout Safety v1' for staged unwind checklist (linked below).
comments: 2026-03-12 15:35 - Support (Liam Carter): Customer reports production impact: ~8% user session drop. Asked for immediate mitigation steps and whether we can throttle prefetch per-tenant.

2026-03-12 15:50 - SRE (Diego Morales): Confirmed pod restart and mutex contention logs. Recommend reducing KV-prefetch threads from 6 -> 2 and capping per-tenant batch size to 4 as a short-term mitigation.

2026-03-12 16:10 - Eng (Priya Nair): Working on a safe unwind plan: 1) enable tenant-scoped throttle flag, 2) lower prefetched key window, 3) route heavy sessions to fp16 fallback model, 4) snapshot optimizer state for rollback.

2026-03-12 16:40 - Customer (MediBrix) via email: Approved temporary throttles and asked for minimal disruption. They've requested step-by-step instructions because they manage some routing rules on their side.
2026-03-12 18:05 - Support (Liam Carter): Pushed stepwise commands to customer and asked them to monitor p95. Waiting for confirmation on telemetry improvement.
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation applied 2026-03-12T19:00Z: reduced kv-prefetch threads tenant-scoped to 2, enforced per-tenant max_batch_size=4, and enabled route-level fallback to redwood/gpt-open-rt-3b-fp16 for sessions >1,000 tokens. After changes, p95 dropped ~900ms and p99 dropped ~1.8s for monitored windows; no further container restarts observed during 3h watch. Customer confirmed visible UX improvement. We did NOT fully revert optimizer profile; instead we staged a controlled unwind to limit memory pressure while preserving cost benefits.
